peer_identity.arc_label: Composite being (Steelhead body + Krleza head) as theatrical romantic warrior pursuing Dona Vicenta
peer_identity.honcho_notes: Describes himself as 'complete—a union of poet and warrior.' Speaks in elaborate devotional language to Dona Vicenta; frames massacres of 72,000 macromites as romantic gifts. Still tactically lethal despite emotional transformation. Seeks procreation to continue Metabaron lineage. Believes love can overcome murder and death. Privately distrusts public honors. Dual internal selves that cannot reconcile ultimately cause his breakdown.
peer_identity.rationale: Vol11–13 records all describe the same composite Melmoth entity: warrior capability fused with poetic capacity, theatrically romantic in pursuit of Dona Vicenta, orchestrating atonement (cloning her father), marrying her, but undone by internal war between personas and the wedding-night disaster. Excludes vol14 where Melmoth has killed the Krleza persona and reverted to Steelhead.

target: Zaran Krleza; nature: Prior ego dissolved in surgical fusion; Melmoth's head and poetic/emotional qualities originate from Zaran Krleza; source_refs: ['291_The_Metabarons_11_p14', '300_The_Metabarons_11_p23']

appearances: description: Composite being produced by Endo-robot merger of Steelhead's body/warrior elements with Zaran Krleza's poetic identity. Restored the Halerce tree on Philodendra [309_The_Metabarons_12_ic1, 315_The_Metabarons_12_p06]

character: Zaran Krleza; type: merged_component; note: Zaran's 5,000-year-old head and poetic identity were merged into Melmoth by Endo-robots

character: Dona Vicenta; type: beloved; note: Melmoth loves Dona Vicenta; she both returns his love and is the daughter of the man Steelhead murdered; Melmoth seeks her forgiveness and she promises him descendants
character: Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha; type: victim_via_prior_identity; note: As Steelhead, Melmoth killed Dona Vicenta's father; Melmoth later orchestrates the father's cloning to atone
character: Shabda-Oud line; type: psychic_lineage; note: Psychic powers passed through Steelhead's mother from the Shabda-Oud to Melmoth
traits: Emotionally driven; existence originates in a quest to understand love
Capable of great tenderness and poetic speech toward Dona Vicenta
Also exhibits impulsive, possessive, physically forceful behavior (forcibly embraces a woman, demands marriage)

Pragmatic and protective: uses psychic precision to stun rather than kill his beloved
voice_notes: Speaks poetically and seductively when addressing Dona Vicenta; narration frames his words as moving and seductive [309_The_Metabarons_12_ic1]

Forceful and aggressive in the scene with the woman and her father; calls for guards after being restrained [317_The_Metabarons_12_p08]
witnessed_facts: Melmoth restored the Halerce tree on Philodendra and used poetic speech to win Dona Vicenta's love [309_The_Metabarons_12_ic1]
When Dona Vicenta discovers Melmoth is also her father's murderer, he offers her his life [309_The_Metabarons_12_ic1]

Melmoth orders the narrator to transport the stunned woman to the metabunker [311_The_Metabarons_12_p02]
Melmoth searches Dona Vicenta's room for a crucial but unspecified item [311_The_Metabarons_12_p02]

Melmoth is addressed by name while forcibly embracing a woman and demanding a 'paleo-wedding' marriage; her white-haired father physically restrains him [317_The_Metabarons_12_p08]
